Hotline Miami
Incredibly fast paced and trippy murder simulator, but also a great experience at the same time. Just try it. Slam the dude with the door then jump on him and bash his head into the floor. Another guy came in - quick just throw your gun at him to knock him out! Grab his knife and sneak out to slice someone else's throat...

 

Talos Principle
This discount doesn't seem very deep, you might want to wait for the Steam Summer Sale in July and see if they give a better deal. The game itself is pretty good though - but a bit easy in my opinion.

The genre is similar to Portal, and they do a pretty good job of easing you into every mechanic, which probably makes it seem even easier than it really is, though I still feel like they take too long to add in the really advanced mechanics.

 

Banished
For a few hours this is an interesting city building/city survival experience, but after that flaws with the population and mechanics start to come through that ruin the long-term experience. It also doesn't cater to large-scale city design, so I'm not sure that it really has the replayability found in normal city building games.

 

Legend of Grimrock The sequel for this game is out, and it's better in every way - but this is still a decent buy if you want to test the genre and see if you enjoy it. There aren't too many games that combine grid-based movement with real time combat, and it has a unique feel.

This game is all in a dark dungeon though - so if you're looking for beautiful outside environments you'll have to play the sequel.

 

Legend of Grimrock 2
An excellent sequel to Legend of Grimrock. The first game was all inside a dark dungeon, and this one expands to a colorful outside world - while still keeping the semi-turn based grid combat.

This is the best game I've played in the party-dungeon-crawler genre, and I'd heartily recommend giving it a shot if you like these. It has some light puzzles to keep everything interesting as well.

 

Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition
A lot of people love the Dark Souls series, it's one of those games you'll either love or hate. Personally I didn't enjoy it - the basic enemies respawn when you die or use a save point, and this makes attempting to kill a boss multiple times kind of a hassle.

Imagine having to reclear trash every time you wanted to kill a boss in World of Warcraft, that would be insanely tedious. Additionally if you want to play the game you'll need to mod it, since the resolution is locked to something atrociously low. You'll also want a game controller, the keyboard is known to be subpar for this game.

So pick this one up if you have a lot of patience, and get satisfaction from trying hard challenges and eventually beating them. Otherwise you may want to give it a pass.

 

Bioshock Triple Pack
BioShock 1 is an FPS with a great atmosphere and unique environment, the only thing I really had an issue with were the big daddies - which were frustrating to fight.

Infinite had combat that was very similar to a normal FPS, and again had an interesting world. Additionally you get a brilliant AI companion, although mid-game it does start feeling a bit fetch-questish.

 

Darksiders
The world in this hack-n-slash is pretty cool, and the weapons are satisfying. It is quite linear, but they designed it well enough that it doesn't feel like a corridor - and I actually got a good Legend Of Zelda vibe from it. If you like those type of games this series might be worth a look.

 

Red Faction Collection
I've only played Red Faction 1 and Armageddon, but the whole series is really known for how destructable the environments are in the games. The first one is quite old and pretty innovative in that respect, you can tunnel through most of the rock in the game using your weapons.

Armageddon prevents terrain destruction but even massive buildings can be knocked down, and it's pretty cool to see - although the camera is a tight-third person view like console games. That makes it a bit more annoying than it should be.

The enemies in this game are pretty easy, and in many places you can just run past them until you hit one of the numerous cutscenes (which despawns everything chasing you). Weapons are also limited, 4 slots. It's very obviously a console experience, and has a lot of strange design decisions that seem more like they were focused on the technical aspects of the game instead of making sure it was fun.

 

Shadow Warrior
A first person hack-n-slash with a humorous protagonist. The story is a ludicrous Japanese tale of ninjas and demons, but the main draw is your character's sardonic remarks about the situation. The swordplay is pretty solid as well.

 

Walking Dead
Obviously this series is known for having a good story - it's basically a choose your own adventure game with point-and-click elements. The downside is that a lot of your choices have no real relevance to the story - often they just choose which of your companions is present during the journey, not what actually happens.

This lack of actual choice was a bit disappointing, but the story is still interesting - so if linearity doesn't bother you it may still be worth a look.

 

Mark of the Ninja
This wasn't a bad game, but I didn't enjoy the feel of it - that ninja feeling just didn't come through for me.

(REVIEWS CONTINUED 1)

 

Outlast

Horror that's more frustrating than scary - I spent most of the time cheesing the enemies by running in circles rather than wasting an absurd amount of time hiding. There are only one or two jump scares, and the game didn't really get good until the very last level in my opinion.

If all the levels had the theme and sense of urgency found in the last level it would have been a far better and more interesting experience.

 

Killing Floor

The sequel to this game is currently in early access (probably for the next 6 months), but for a couple bucks this is a great co-op experience. You fight off hordes of zombies with different special abilities, working to use your classes together. One person might be the sharpshooter, another might take out big enemies with shotguns, and a third person might light all the small ones on fire with a flamethrower.

It's important to level up, because you get perks as you get to higher levels - for example the firebug's smg starts lighting things on fire, and he gets complete immunity to flaming enemies. The only downside is that this leveling can take a long time for some classes - and that's one of the things they're improving in the sequel.

 

Trine2

I actually prefer this original game to the sequel - it felt a lot more like an adventure through a sandbox, rather than the forced linear nature of some of the sequel puzzles. I wouldn't really call it a puzzle game though - most of it is about platforming while killing enemies.

 

Trine

I actually prefer this original game to the sequel - it felt a lot more like an adventure through a sandbox, rather than the forced linear nature of some of the sequel puzzles. I wouldn't really call it a puzzle game though - most of it is about platforming while killing enemies.

 

Limbo

This linear little platformer is a dark journey full of death, and a pretty fun time if you like casual puzzle platforming. It has great atmosphere, and is definitely worth the couple dollar pricetag from this sale.

 

The Fall

This game had terrible controls but was a great experience. It really should have been a point-and-click, but once you get past that the sci-fi atmosphere is really great, and the story is enjoyable.

The basic premise is that you're a sentient space suit whose owner has passed out, and you're trying to rescue him. One of my top picks last year.

 

Braid

I think this was the first game that used time reversal as a crucial mechanic, and the puzzle element of it is pretty good. Since you can reverse time it never gets frustrating when an enemy kills you, just step back a few seconds and try again. The story is a bit weird though and really didn't grab my attention. Even by the end of the game you may not fully understand it.

 

Orcs Must Die 2

This is a decent co-op experience - which the original game didn't have - but it lacks the great sense of humor that game had. And that was what really made the previous one shine in my opinion, without that it's just a solid first-person tower defense.

 

Shadow of Mordor

The gameplay in this was solid, with the overall collectables and roaming feeling very much like Assassin's Creed. The combat was pretty easy - somewhat satisfying but would have been better if there was actually a chance of you dieing in a swarm of enemies. Currently you can just dash around and hop over dudes and be nearly invincible unless you mess up. Fun, but not difficult.

My video review is also based on the main game - there have been DLC that may have completed the story, but the main game itself kind of leaves you hanging.

 

The Swapper

Sure, this is a puzzle game, but the thing that really appealed to me was the atmosphere. They do a great job of making you feel truly alone in an abandoned space, and just for that alone it's worth trying.

 

Just Cause 2

Single-player mayhem with an over-the-top story, this is an all-around great experience. There is a multiplayer mod, but they haven't really fixed the bugs enough for it to be a proper multiplayer experience - I'd still classify this as a mainly single-player game.

It's a really good one though, and if you haven't played it I'd definitely recommend picking it up. Don't worry, it still looks pretty nice even though it came out 5 years ago.

 

Auditorium

This one was a pretty great music puzzle game where you have to arrange circles of sound/color properly to finish the level. It's only $0.69 and I'd highly recommend picking it up if you like music-based games.

 

Dungeon Defenders

There's actually a sequel for this game out now, but the original didn't thrill me. It has some towers but the actually killing usually comes down to the players - but in this case it just feels repetitive. I never felt a real sense of urgency or skill - like Sanctum 2 has - it's just flailing your sword or auto-shooting your wand. Since waves take a while this can become pretty monotonous.

 

Saints Row 4

If you liked Saints Row 3 you'll probably enjoy this one - it's more of the same over-the-top action, but this time you also have superhero powers. Cars and planes are almost obsolete since you can run faster and fly on your own, and this makes getting around much more pleasant. Really it has every activity and character the previous game had, rebranded differently, but has a more comic book flavor.

Oh and the title intro to this game is absolutely fantastic.

 

Rogue Legacy

Definitely a solid game, as long as you like platformers. The twist is that every time you play you choose between a few random characters, and slowly improve your armor and stats. The dungeon layout is different, but the bosses are the same each time.

These random characters obviously have different skills and problems (like color blindness), and this makes each run a unique challenge. It's a well polished experience.

 

Antichamber

This is a wacky mind-bending experience that has plenty of puzzle elements, but feels more like an experience than a straight-forward puzzle game. You won't get to see all the areas of the world unless you can think out of the box. Sometimes backtracking down a hallway does not take you to the same area you just came from, for instance.

The game does a good job of hinting at what you should do though - it doesn't make things obvious, but I never felt frustrated or completely mystified. Usually even if you can't figure out the path you're trying to take, you'll accidentally end up somewhere else unique.

 

140

I quite enjoyed this little abstract platformer, although it is super short (under an hour if I remember correctly). For $0.99 it might be worth giving a shot though - there's also a hardcore mode after you finish - playing all the levels backwards.

 

Reus

You control multiple gods, transforming the environment of a barren planet to help tribes of people flourish. The core of the gameplay is growth objectives for the tribes, which eventually unlock more abilities for your gods. A lot of this revolves around making different combinations of plants, animals, and minerals in the world for the villagers to use.

It's a bit of world building with a slight puzzle feel to it, and I really enjoyed it the first time through. I don't feel like it has a ton of replayability though.

 

SteamWorld Dig

This was a few hours of solid gameplay, although the only thing I found particularly exciting was the final boss fight - which was excellent. The rest of the game was pretty good, but mining gems to buy more equipment and fighting a few enemies probably won't thrill most people. The design was good, it just wasn't particularly challenging.

 

Sleeping Dogs

I know there's a storyline, but my favorite part of this game was just roaming around the massive city. You can drive for an insanely long time without seeing the same scenery, and that's incredibly relaxing and enjoyable.

The combat isn't your normal shooting either, it's combined with martial arts combos and fist-fights, so the experience is somewhat unique. Not your standard GTA type game.

 

Stealth Bastard Deluxe

An excellent platforming experience, this is a remake of the free game by the same name. You can try that one first and see if you like it, this is just more polished with a good introduction and some other features. I bought it mainly to support the dev, since it's a great little game.

 

Contagion

This is primarily a multiplayer game - although you could play a few of the scenario maps solo. These maps are actually my biggest complaint about the multiplayer, because you'll probably be dropping in after the game starts - unless you're playing with friends. When this happens it's pretty hard to find other people, or the objectives, unless you're already very familiar with the maps.

There's also a Last Man Standing mode where dead people become zombies and hunt the living players, and I actually liked hunting better than trying to win. Interesting experience.

(REVIEWS CONTINUED 2)

 

Deus Ex Collection

If you haven't played the Deus Ex series I'd highly recommend buying this. You'll probably want to mod the first two games so that they look better, as they're pretty old.

You can skip playing DX: The Fall, it's terrible and doesn't add anything to the storyline. I've included videos for everything besides Invisible War, which is rather controversial. A lot of people thought it was a bad game, and it's very console-oriented, but story-wise it adds a lot to the series.

 

Vessel

This puzzle-platformer focuses a lot of physics and liquid simulations, and I felt like the platforming and playing a character detracted a bit from the puzzle part. The story is decent though, so the character isn't a total waste, and it has a solid graphical style.

Overall not a game I loved, but if you like puzzle-platfomers this one is okay.

 

Commandos Collection

I picked these up a while ago, but haven't played them a whole lot simply because they feel quite dated. They're very challenging, and lack a lot of modern amenities like good checkpoints. So while you may want to pick them up for nostalgia, keep in mind they may not provide the experience that you remember - gaming has come a long way since then.

 

Brutal Legend

I'm not a fan of the rock groups portrayed in this game, so maybe that would help - but even Jack Black didn't keep me entertained. It wasn't bad but just felt fairly lackluster - a somewhat generic attempt at the open world collectable genre.

 

Machinarium

This point-and-click has a lot of difficult puzzles, not very intuitive in my opinion. It also doesn't distinguish well between background and usable items, which makes solving it evn harder. Not bad, but you really have to enjoy point-and-click puzzles to avoid being frustrated by it.

 

Guns of Icarus Online

I haven't played this one in a while, so some of the balance may have changed, since it is a multiplayer-only game and I think they're constantly tweaking it. Your experience is really going to depend on your crew. Each team picks out a flying ship, with people playing the role of gunner, engineer, and captain, trying to destroy the other team.

It isn't a free-for-all, there are usually a few ships on each side - and there are a number of different ship types too, each with different configurations and types of guns. One of the littlest ones has a flamethrower on the front, for instance.

When I was playing the ship types didn't feel completely balanced, but I think that may just be a matter of experience on how to kill your enemy. Each ship has a few hitboxes, for the ship itself and one for the balloon above - so you have to use strategy targeting different parts.

While the repairers are running around you may want to damage the engines so it can't move, and then your ship can sit out of range and pound them with impunity. Damaging the balloon makes it harder for them to stay aloft, and so on. It's a decent system that can be chaotic fun if your crew is good and your enemies are too, although sometimes it feels like it goes on a bit too long.

 

Van Helsing

This one I haven't reviewed, and only played for an hour or two. It's a Diablo type experience, but felt really unbalanced to me. A lot of the enemies took far too long to die, even in areas where you're on the storyline quest - which should have a clear and proper balance. Maybe it gets better later in the game, but I wasn't willing to play it for several more hours to find out.

 

Super Meat Boy

Everyone should know this game by now - but if you don't, it's a good hardcore precision platformer. The controls are tight and feel satisfying, and the levels are challenging but fair. If you hit a spike or spinning saw blade you get sent back to the start, and once you finally complete the level you can watch all your ghosts go at once, in a flood of bloody explosions. It's very cathartic.

 

EvE

It's been a few expansions since I've played this MMO, but it really was a weird experience. You need to be interested in joining a social group (corporation) or you won't get far in this game - it has pretty heavy griefing and favors older players.

Leveling up is done over time, not by grinding - you just pick your skills and they train in so many hours, days, or weeks. So you can't be flying the biggest ships right off the bat, but if you want to pursue only that skill it won't take an absurd amount of time either. If you want every skill that will take a while though.

Combat and movement feel a bit more like playing a text adventure, but it has pretty visuals to keep you invested. You don't really steer, just set trajectories (circling the enemy) or waypoints and fire your guns when they come off cooldown. All the while you're watching your power levels, making sure your opponent doesn't warp away, etc.

It's a complex and unique experience, but emphasizes being a griefer if you enjoy that, and grouping up with others to protect yourself if you hate it.

 

Hammerwatch

I gave this dungeon crawler a try a while ago, and just didn't find it very compelling (on top of the controls being a bit rough - you can only aim straight). This made it a bit slower than it should have been, but still wasn't particularly challenging. Cute pixel graphics, mediocre gameplay.

 

Risk of Rain

The concept is solid but this game has a lot of technical issues, even if you aren't recording. If you are trying to record it's even worse since it doesn't play well with FRAPS or Dxtory (though I've heard that OBS sometimes works). It's a fun co-op experience, mowing down waves of monsters, grabbing loot and upgrades for your character - but the lag when the game gets busier can ruin this.

The Black Sorcerer Is In Town by Sabastien Hue

before i even start the story, absolutely badass image, dude. moving on though

alleyway council policy was a freeing thing at this day and age. not that they would be so okay with Arthurs disdain for stealth fields, but he had picked a dead part of town at a dead hour. their policy now, was strong enough to shatter the shackles of the containment organizations, allow the odd and the mystical to flourish, but not strong enough to do anything to him if he kept this quiet.

and, he wasn't even a days walk away from their main headquarters, yet not even the infamous wanderer had objected to him making here, a regular walkaround. not in the sense he had a regular source of extortable income here. but, these streets, the skies above them, that now flashed with intermittent lightning, were his by force. even if the next decades ended that, this was the present.

and that boundary was quite recognized. a fact that made Arthur proud, even as a shade of fan-boy reflected that the wanderer would have called him a tosser. he stopped in his patrol as he rounded the cobbled corner. the old woman waiting for him was not a regular here. but, she eyed him too knowingly, unafraid of the lit tinge of red, announcing power and magic that could turn her inside out, and bind her soul to prearranged brokers that spoke equally with necromancers, and bankers in the bowels of civilian bank offices.

she rose up to speak with him. standing on the edges of his territory, he held on to an understanding of power, that would have made a lot of weaker men tremble. "you look like you want to speak" he said, aiming for the confidence held in bar folk tales as figureheads opened ranges held empty for centuries until a faction powerful enough, took them anyways. she said "yes, the alleyway ones did not listen, for they accepted it anyway", she had that premeditated feel of a fortune teller, and the forward nature of the encounter echoed it.

the future and causality were an implicit boundary in the community, but Arthur said "alright, what did they ignore?". she said "this will not last, it will end, and the pillars will find bigger fortunes in man rather then ghosts and temporal twists. powers will change and only when united states shatter into pieces and new glory will form, will the cards be bare". Arthur didn't have a response. he didn't know whether to send her away, or thank for the morsel, or cower.
